sampling_model.design: Independent samples are drawn from one target population and from each edge-indexed randomized trial; in trial \(e\), treatment is assigned with probability \(1/2\) to each endpoint of \(e\).
sampling_model.units: Each trial unit contributes \((A,Y,X,W,Z_e)\), and each target unit contributes \((X,W)\); all alphabets are fixed and finite.
sampling_model.treatment: The treatment set is \(V=\{0,\ldots,k\}\), with treatment \(0\) the root and the observed randomized comparisons encoded by a directed multigraph \(G=(V,E)\).
sampling_model.overlap: All observed complete cells are at least \(\eta>0\), and each sampling proportion converges to a positive limit.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cell frequencies estimate each \(A_{P,x}\), the block-diagonal \(A_P\), \(b_P\), and \(R_0\). A fixed spectral cutoff is used only on a separated-rank class; the exact confidence projection evaluates \(A_p,b_p,R_p\) jointly at every candidate table and uses no estimated rank.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 2.3 states that a linear bridge functional is identified if and only if its representer annihilates the operator nullspace.
Proposition 2 identifies the target contrast from any solution of either observed bridge equation in a two-trial indirect comparison.
The finite-proxy causal effect is identified under a full-rank proxy matrix without identification of the measurement mechanism.
The tree-packing theorem characterizes \(q\) edge-disjoint spanning trees by partition cut inequalities.
The matroid partition theorem gives the classical union-rank min--max formula through disjoint independent sets.
Theorem 1 expresses orthogonally invariant treatment-design criteria through the spectrum of a vertex-weighted graph Laplacian.
A strongly identified linear functional admits root-\(n\) asymptotically normal inference despite a weakly identified conditional-moment nuisance.
Proxy variables yield causal-effect bounds without completeness or point identification of a bridge.
Calibrated projection yields uniformly asymptotically valid confidence intervals for scalar projections of moment-identified parameters.
Causally interpretable meta-analysis transports treatment effects from multiple randomized trials using observed effect modifiers.
Regression-based proximal reconciliation compares two trials under parametric latent effect-modification models.
Conditional Wald critical values are robust to arbitrarily weak identification and non-homoskedastic errors in IV and nonlinear GMM.

body.tldr: A finite network of randomized treatment comparisons can identify transported root contrasts even when every trial-specific proxy bridge is nonunique. The paper's kernel is a causal nullity theorem: under finite binary outcomes and a support-tangent condition that permits structural zeros, the target vector is identified if and only if \(\ker(A_P)\subseteq\ker(R_0)\), and every violation is realized by an explicit two-sided family of observationally equivalent full-data laws. Stratum-specific operators \(A_{P,x}\) make the second headline precise: attainable rows from a rank-\(q_x\) common proxy kernel generically reach rank \(q_x(|V|-1)\) exactly at the \(q_x\)-tree threshold, with global rank equal to the sum across strata. Classical matroid union then certifies a concrete minimum-cost trial augmentation; separated-rank Wald inference and exact candidate-law projection provide complementary uncertainty guarantees.

project_justification.gap: Zhang et al. characterize invariance of a linear functional over a statistical bridge fiber, and Su et al. identify one transported two-trial contrast. Neither result proves that each target-relevant bridge null direction corresponds to two support-feasible causal completions that preserve every observed trial cell and the shared latent contrast restrictions in an arbitrary treatment network.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is the causal tangent space of a finite proximal trial network: algebraic nonuniqueness must be lifted through potential-outcome kernels while holding the full observed law fixed. Its dimension and its interaction with treatment-graph connectivity determine which new trials can add causal information.
project_justification.fill: The project constructs a support-restricted signed-cell lift for every null direction, derives the exact annihilator criterion and local ambiguity dimension, and proves that rows attainable from a common stochastic proxy kernel realize the classical tree-packing rank threshold in each stratum. Classical matroid union is used only to certify a new causal network-augmentation consequence. Regular inference on separated rank strata and conservative exact candidate-law projection complete the analysis.

body.related_work: The affine-solution insight comes from \cite{ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023}, whose Proposition 2.3 identifies a linear functional when it annihilates the bridge nullspace; the present kernel addresses the stronger causal question by realizing every violating direction through support-feasible full-data completions. \cite{SuRytgaardRavnEriksson2026} supplies a two-trial proximal indirect-comparison formula, while the multistratum example has four treatments, cycles, and collective rank unavailable from a single indirect comparison. \cite{MiaoGengTchetgen2018} supplies the finite-proxy matrix-rank perspective, but the example remains contrast-identified in a stratum with \(q_x<d\). \cite{DahabrehRobertsonPetitoHernanSteingrimsson2023} transports effects from multiple trials using observed effect modifiers; it does not certify the example with a latent modifier and proxy restrictions. \cite{XuEtAl2026} studies two-trial proximal reconciliation under parametric latent effect-modification models and is informative rather than a theorem-level target. The graph threshold uses the classical tree-packing result of \cite{NashWilliams1961} and the classical matroid-partition result of \cite{Edmonds1965}; neither certificate nor the projection operation is presented as new. \cite{Rosa2018} informs precision design after attainable rank is settled. The separated-rank estimator is informed by \cite{BennettEtAl2023}, and exact Clopper--Pearson cell projection is a conservative finite-sample complement to \cite{KaidoMolinariStoye2019}. \cite{SotiropoulosEtAl2024} supplies the NETMOTION consumer, where a low-rank proxy stratum can bind before additional graph connectivity does.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact causal converse is restricted to finite binary outcomes, a public finite latent-support bound, strictly positive common \(W\)-given-\(U\) kernels, and conditional potential-outcome supports spanning every anchor-zero one-way marginal increment used by the lift. The latter permits structural zeros but excludes support faces with deficient anchor-zero tangent rank. Tree packing, matroid union, and the deterministic projection argument are classical; novelty rests on the support-feasible causal lift, the attainable common-proxy-row representation, and their network-augmentation implication. The exact confidence set may be conservative, nonconvex, or nonshrinking near rank changes.
body.honest_scope: The support-restricted signed-cell lift, exact nullity equivalence, local ambiguity dimension, attainable common-row rank theorem, multistratum example, causal augmentation consequence, and two inference guarantees are theorem targets. The support-face extension remains open when the one-way support-tangent map is not surjective or the common proxy kernel has zeros. Under one source edge, one target population, and a target functional that annihilates the bridge kernel, the observable formula reduces to the any-solution proximal transport formula of \cite{SuRytgaardRavnEriksson2026}. In a stratum with \(q_x=d\) and \(d\) edge-disjoint spanning trees, the graph result reduces to ordinary full-column-rank bridge recovery; with \(q_x<d\), it respects the finite-proxy rank ceiling of \cite{MiaoGengTchetgen2018}. The NETMOTION application is conditional on valid harmonized proxies and an independent target sample.
